papers.title: Direct Joule-Heated Non-Equilibrium Synthesis Enables High Performing Thermoelectrics
papers.abstract: High-throughput synthesis of bulk inorganic materials is crucial for accelerating functional materials discovery but is hindered by slow, energy-intensive solid-state methods. We introduce Direct Joule-Heated Synthesis (DJS), a rapid, single-step and scalable solid-state synthesis technique achieving a $10^5$-fold speedup and 20,000x energy efficiency improvement over conventional synthesis. DJS enables the synthesis of dense, bulk chalcogenides ($\mathrm{Bi_{0.5}Sb_{1.5}Te_3}$, $\mathrm{AgSbTe_2}$), achieving a zT of 2.3 at 573 K in optimally Cd/Se co-doped $\mathrm{AgSbTe_2}$, one of the highest for polycrystalline materials at this temperature. DJS enables optimal co-doping and rapid, non-equilibrium solidification, producing lamellar microstructures, interfacial regions, and cation-ordered nanodomains that scatter all-scale phonons, achieving ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (~0.2 $W m^{-1} K^{-1}$ at 573 K). DJS establishes a new benchmark for scalable and fast synthesis, accelerating functional material discovery.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本论文聚焦热电材料合成，与用户研究方向（生物打印、髋关节植入物、FEA代理模型、生物医学增材制造）完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is about thermoelectric material synthesis and thermoelectric performance, with no biomedical context, no implant mechanics, no additive manufacturing for biomedical applications, and no FEA surrogate modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 加速功能材料发现，解决传统固相合成慢且耗能的问题
summary_zh.method: 提出直接焦耳加热合成（DJS），实现快速、单步、可扩展的体相材料合成
summary_zh.result: 在Cd/Se共掺杂AgSbTe2中实现zT达2.3（573 K），并形成多尺度纳米结构
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验表征热电性能（电导率、Seebeck系数、热导率）验证

summary_en.motivation: To accelerate the discovery of functional inorganic materials by overcoming the slow and energy-intensive nature of conventional solid-state synthesis.
summary_en.method: A single-step, scalable Direct Joule-Heated Synthesis (DJS) technique is introduced for rapid bulk chalcogenide synthesis, enabling non-equilibrium solidification.
summary_en.result: Optimally Cd/Se co-doped AgSbTe2 achieves a zT of 2.3 at 573 K, attributed to all-scale phonon scattering from lamellar microstructures and nanodomains.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of electrical and thermal transport properties confirm the high thermoelectric performance and microstructure features.
